safetyRemovalDialog.title: Safety Factor Source Removed
safetyRemovalDialog.message:
The safety annotations that automatically enabled the Safety Impact factor have been removed from the DFD and Asset Tab. Do you want to keep the Safety Impact factor active?

Keeping it preserves existing safety ratings. Removing it will clear all safety factor values from your risk assessments.

config.title: Risk Assessment Configuration
config.complexDesc: Separate Impact and Likelihood factors. More detailed analysis, industry standard methodologies.
config.showIndividualFactorsDesc: When disabled, only aggregated Impact/Likelihood values are shown. Hover shows details.
config.roundingCeilDesc: Always rounds up to higher risk level
config.useAssetImpact: Pre-fill Impact from Asset Tab data
config.useAssetImpactDesc: Impact factors are pre-filled from linked asset criteria (1:1 match by ID). The analyst can override any value — an 'Overridden' chip marks values that differ from the derived value.
config.assetImpactMappingDesc: Used when no per-criterion data is available for a factor.
config.assetImpactMappingHint: Default mapping resets when scale changes.
config.severityThresholdsHint: Scores above the highest threshold always map to the last level.
config.safetyAutoEnabledTooltip: Automatically enabled — safety annotations detected in DFD or Asset Tab. Disable manually to exclude safety impact from risk scoring.

eliminate.label: Eliminate
eliminate.description: Remove the risk source entirely — the vulnerability or attack vector is fully resolved by the selected countermeasures. No residual risk remains.

reduce.label: Reduce
reduce.description: Lower the likelihood or impact through targeted countermeasures. A residual risk remains but is brought to an acceptable level.

accept.label: Accept
accept.description: Consciously retain the risk without implementing countermeasures. The risk is within defined tolerance thresholds. Justification required.

transfer.label: Transfer
transfer.description: Shift full responsibility for the risk to a third party (e.g. via insurance, contractual liability clause, or outsourcing). Justification required.

share.label: Share
share.description: Distribute responsibility across multiple parties — e.g. part of the countermeasure is implemented in the product, part in the surrounding system or operator procedures. Justification required.

should.label: Should
should.description: Important - should be addressed if possible

could.label: Could
could.description: Nice to have - could be addressed

wont.label: Won't
wont.description: Accepted risk - won't be addressed this iteration

damage_potential.name: Damage Potential
damage_potential.description: How much damage could result from the threat?

reproducibility.name: Reproducibility
reproducibility.description: How easy is it to reproduce the attack?

exploitability.name: Exploitability
exploitability.description: How much skill is needed to exploit the vulnerability?

discoverability.name: Discoverability
discoverability.description: How easy is it to discover the vulnerability?

skill_level.name: Skill Level
skill_level.description: How technically skilled is the attacker?

opportunity.name: Opportunity
opportunity.description: What resources and opportunities are required?

size.name: Size
size.description: How large is the group of potential attackers?

ease_of_discovery.name: Ease of Discovery
ease_of_discovery.description: How easy is it to find the vulnerability?

ease_of_exploit.name: Ease of Exploit
ease_of_exploit.description: How easy is it to actually exploit the vulnerability?

awareness.name: Awareness
awareness.description: How well known is the vulnerability?

intrusion_detection.name: Intrusion Detection
intrusion_detection.description: How likely is detection of an exploit?

window_of_opportunity.name: Window of Opportunity (WoO)
window_of_opportunity.description: How long is the vulnerability accessible to an attacker?

attacker_capability.name: Attacker Capability (AC)
attacker_capability.description: Skill level, motivation and resources of a potential attacker.

exposure_level.name: Exposure Level (EL)
exposure_level.description: How exposed is the asset or system to potential attackers?

financial_damage.name: Financial Damage
financial_damage.description: How much financial damage would result from a successful attack?

regulatory_compliance.name: Regulatory & Compliance
regulatory_compliance.description: How much regulatory exposure or compliance violation would result?

reputation.name: Reputation Damage
reputation.description: How severely would the organisation's reputation be affected?

privacy.name: Privacy Violation
privacy.description: How much personally identifiable information could be exposed?

operational.name: Operational Impact
operational.description: How much operational disruption or service loss would result?

affected_users.name: Affected Users
affected_users.description: How many persons, customers, machines or plants are affected when this vulnerability is successfully exploited? 1 = single user/machine, 2 = multiple systems at the same customer, 3 = many customers / all installations of a product type, 4 = cross-customer / supply-chain-wide.

recoverability.name: Recoverability
recoverability.description: How difficult is it to recover from the impact? 1 = fully recoverable, 4 = unrecoverable / permanent damage.

accountability.name: Accountability Loss
accountability.description: How much is the traceability of actions compromised?

safety.name: Safety Impact
safety.description: What is the potential harm to persons? 1 = reversible minor injury, 2 = reversible moderate, 3 = irreversible injury, 4 = fatality. Aligned with ISO 12100 / EN 50742.

physical_damage.name: Physical Damage
physical_damage.description: How much physical damage to hardware, infrastructure or property would result?

environmental.name: Environmental Impact
environmental.description: What environmental harm could result (spills, emissions, contamination)?

supply_chain.name: Supply Chain Impact
supply_chain.description: How severely would the supply chain or production pipeline be disrupted?

loss_of_confidentiality.name: Loss of Confidentiality
loss_of_confidentiality.description: How much data could be disclosed?

loss_of_integrity.name: Loss of Integrity
loss_of_integrity.description: How much data could be corrupted?

loss_of_availability.name: Loss of Availability
loss_of_availability.description: How much service could be lost?

loss_of_accountability.name: Loss of Accountability
loss_of_accountability.description: Are actions traceable to the attacker?

privacy_violation.name: Privacy Violation
privacy_violation.description: How much personally identifiable information affected?

deployment_scope.name: Deployment Scope
deployment_scope.description: Can a single successful attack simultaneously compromise multiple installations? 1 = no — each installation must be attacked individually, 2 = partially — attack affects multiple systems at the same customer, 3 = yes — shared infrastructure (cloud, OTA, SCADA) affects all installations of a product type simultaneously, 4 = yes — supply-chain attack compromises all customers at once.
